findings.topic: Model catch-up release 1 (D-MDL-01): retired tags kept in place, A-1000 / A-2000 tanks at datasheet volumes

findings.observation: D-MDL-01 (bases MC-1–MC-10, approved by QFL 2026-09-28) brings the model in line with the V219–V227 data-layer decisions. Release 1 keeps the 21 retired A-1000 / A-2000 tags in place — shown grey and labelled RETIRED with their decision — because the model engineer's validators still assert their streams, and resizes the A-1000 / A-2000 tanks to the issued datasheets (T-1006 400 m³ at Ø 8.4 m, R-1001 25, R-1002 30, R-1003 16, R-1004 10, T-1002 80, T-1003 30, T-1008 12, T-2001 15, T-2002 100 m³). Against main, on A-1000 / A-2000: pipe-support holds 229 → 230, structure passes, no headroom conflict, and two more reserved-space entries on an existing class in the containment yard (BND-1004 / TR-perimeter-85); R-1002 / R-1003 / R-1004 keep their footprints because new diameters re-flowed rack supports into emergency walkways PW-ES-030 / 031. Current model: 107 holds plant-wide. C-301 and T-304 (release 2) sit behind the pipe-racks-v31 fixture, which already fails on main.
findings.action: Model engineer: remove the retired tags and rebaseline the validators and the pipe-racks-v31 fixture (docs/model-catchup-handoff.md); then release 2 (C-301 filter press, new equipment in existing areas) and release 3 (A-1100, A-5400 envelope).

findings.topic: Thermal-oil mains A-5400 → HX-601 on a dedicated rack (D-MDL-05)
findings.status: Applied — position superseded by LAY-16; stress and vendor checks open
findings.observation: D-MDL-05 (bases M5-1–M5-10, approved by QFL 2026-10-01): the A-5400 screening boxes are replaced by real-world equipment on the same 10 × 18 m pad — H-5400 a horizontal cylindrical coil heater Ø 3.6 × 10 m on saddles with burner, FD fan, gas train, top walkway and ladder, flue box and Ø 1.4 m stack to ≈ 20 m with sampling platform; P-5401A/B horizontal end-suction hot-oil pumps with motors on baseplates; V-5401 a Ø 1.8 × 4.5 m expansion drum (≈ 11 m³) on a frame above the loop high point with deck and ladder, and an air separator on the pump suction (untagged until LST-001 allocates one); T-5401 a Ø 2.6 × 6 m drain drum (≈ 30 m³) at grade (N₂-push drain-down). The package is piped (return → air separator → pumps → coil → supply; expansion, overflow, drain-down, refill), and DN300 insulated supply and return mains (≈ 65 m each, stacked at 7.4 / 6.6 m below the A-5000 utility racks) run on a dedicated T-post rack (12 posts) into the HX-601 battery limits BL-HT601-IN / -RET, which are no longer blinded; under Route 2 + 6 a DN150 branch (≈ 45 m each way, 6 more posts) serves PK-1101 stage 2. Built with the catch-up equipment after the plant-wide support generator, so no other rack re-flows; no clash with existing parts under either acid route. The corridor came from an occupancy scan of the built model: along x 105, z 5.45 (between the A-5000 rack columns at z 4.65 and 6.0, clear of the WATER-FRONT and WALK-601 walkways) and x 78.3 (east of the PL-601 stair tower). The rack is explicit, so the generated supports and holds are untouched — current model: 107 holds plant-wide. Open: HX-601’s heating nozzles and local heating routes are DN100 placeholders in the A-600 model (reducers at the battery limit) against 543 / 597 m³/h of oil (DAT-065 V1.3); the stack height waits for the dispersion study; no pipe-stress, expansion or hydraulic calculation; equipment dimensions are model choices pending vendor data (U8).
findings.action: Pipe-stress / expansion review of the ≈ 65 m runs and anchor / guide positions at detailed design; confirm the rack against the site traffic plan; re-run this review when the vendor package (U8) and HX-601 nozzle sizes arrive.

findings.topic: Forklift unloading: a pallet of four chemical drums placed in A-100 drum staging bay SB-1
findings.status: Proposed — chemical, containment and operating plan open
findings.observation: V321 (QFL 2026-10-08: receiving → A-100 first, chemical drums, electric truck only; the spot was selected by the model engineer). The route receiving-unload carries one 1.2 × 1.2 m pallet of four 205 L drums from the receiving point through the west vehicle door and along the aisle at z −6.8, turns left (3.5 m path radius) into bay SB-1 at (−19, −1.6) (truck stop at (−19, −2.6)), lowers and places the pallet, withdraws the forks 1.4 m, raises them and reverses back to the door: 91.2 m of travel, 456 screening positions, no modeled obstruction in screened envelope. The bay is the only free floor near the A-100 frontage that clears the swept path with both the forklift and the generic transport profile (x −17.5 to −19); it is about 0.3 m from the thermal-delivery lane envelope (x −17). The 1.6 m containment pad, the marking and the sign are a display aid in the tracing view, not a model equipment record. Open: the chemical, its hazard class and segregation (acid or oxidiser), the containment volume for four drums and the BC Fire Code container rules (not checked); drum and pallet mass against the truck rating; the delivery truck and dock; charging; the traffic plan and the pedestrian crossing at the west door (the preview stops the truck for the pedestrian).
findings.action: Confirm the chemical and its hazard class, then size the containment pad, decide segregation and check the container rules; record SB-1 as a model equipment record once agreed; confirm the pallet mass against the truck rating; plan the thermal-delivery lane around a staged pallet.

findings.topic: A-5400 thermal-oil package outside the east wall; perimeter road rerouted (V315–V320)
findings.status: Applied — wind, vendor and road approval open
findings.observation: V315–V319 (QFL 2026-10-07 and 08): the A-5400 package, which D-MDL-05 (LAY-14) placed inside the east wall, now stands outside it: pad x 124–135.2, z −24 to −4.5 (11.1 × 19.4 m; 6.4 m from the outer face of the east wall, about 16 m from the A-800 block edge, 41 m from PY-801 and 22 m from A-900). The two DN300 mains run north from the pad, turn west on the z 5.45 line and pass straight through the wall, one penetration each, to x 78.3; the old jog along x 105 is gone. The perimeter logistics circuit was rerouted around the pad ((125, −30) → (142, −30) → (142, 1.5) → (125, 1.5), lane edges about 3 m from the curb), its south leg steps in to z −40 east of the retention bunds (x 76) and it starts at the A-800 east frontage (125, 23) (V320): no modeled obstruction in screened envelope, 579 m, 2811 positions. The position, the BC Fire Code and regulation register CR-1 to CR-10 and the distances are tracked in the A-5400 assembly and design review (CR-4, the containment clearance, is met in the model after the V318 widening). Open: prevailing wind and the site boundary east of x 140; the road reroute is a proposal, not an approved roadway; an 11 m rack span over the road for the 0.52 m insulated mains needs a structural check; HX-601 duty against the DN300 → DN100 reducer; several fire-code article numbers are marked to confirm.
findings.action: Confirm the position with the HAZOP and the fire authority, record the CR-1 to CR-10 reviews, check the rack span over the road, approve or revise the road reroute, and re-run this review when the vendor package (U8) arrives.
